items.title: Inflation worsened last month to 3.7% in sign that prices remain elevated as midterm elections near
items.excerpt: (AP) - WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gasoline and many other goods and services became more expensive, evidence that rising prices remain an economic challenge just a few weeks before midterm elections that have focused heavily on affordability. The consumer price index rose 3.7% in September compared with a year ago, the Labor Department said Wednesday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, costs jumped 0.6% from August to September, the biggest gain in five months, up from a 0.4% increase the previous month. ... Excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 2.6% in September from a year ago, up from 2.4% the previous month and higher than economists had expected. And they climbed 0.3% from August to September, an elevated pace that, if it continued for a year, would run well above the Fed’s 2% target. ... Higher inflation will likely put more pressure on the Fed to lift its key interest rate at its next meeting Oct. 27-28. Economists noted that the report showed price increases were spread more broadly across the economy than in recent months. ... Federal Reserve officials are watching inflation data closely to determine whether they need to raise their short-term interest rate further, and by how much. ... Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said last month that inflation isn’t moving quickly enough back to the central bank’s target, causing the Fed to hike rates for the first time in three years, to about 3.9%. ... Yet some key Fed officials have suggested the central bank can wait before increasing rates again. The Fed has a policy meeting Oct. 27-28, but most Wall Street investors expect it to hold rates then, and potentially implement another hike in December. Fed officials have penciled in just one more rate hike this year. ... Still, Wednesday’s report has led many Wall Street investors to project that the Fed will now act in two weeks. The odds of a rate increase at the central bank’s October meeting have doubled, though remain at just 50-50, according to futures pricing tracked by CME Fedwatch. ... Stock prices fell slightly after the report, while greater expectations for rate hikes pushed up bond yields, which will raise borrowing costs throughout the economy.

items.title: Inflation is retreating from most of the store — why your biggest bills are the holdouts: Chart of the Day
items.excerpt: Inflation is retreating from most of the store — why your biggest bills are the holdouts: Chart of the Day # Inflation is retreating from most of the store — why your biggest bills are the holdouts: Chart of the Day Jared Blikre Sun, October 18, 2026 at 6:33 AM CDT 3 min read Inflation is reaching fewer corners of the economy. That doesn't mean life is getting cheaper. Only about 38% of the roughly 175 categories in the Consumer Price Index rose faster than a 3% annual pace over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance calculations from Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data. That's down from 56% in May and the fewest since spring 2025. The count borrows a test from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who laid it out at Jackson Hole in August. He counts how many categories in the Fed's preferred PCE price gauge are rising faster than 3%, a gauge of how widespread inflation is. The Fed's goal is still 2%. BLS, Yahoo Finance "Too many categories are still posting increases above 3% on both a six- and 12-month basis," Warsh said after the Fed raised rates in September. By that yardstick, September looked better than its hotter-than-expected headline. The 12-month count slipped to about 47% from 51% in August. At the 2022 peak, about 4 in 5 categories topped 3%. In the two decades before the pandemic, about 1 in 3 typically did. A narrower spread strengthens the case for waiting, and traders have leaned that way. The bond market put the odds of a hike at the Oct. 27-28 meeting at about 17% by Friday's close, according to Bloomberg data — down from roughly 33% after Wednesday's CPI report. Warsh declined to preview his next move in remarks Friday before the International Monetary Fund. Some Fed officials want more evidence before moving. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called September's inflation report discouraging but told Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger he favors waiting before acting again. "We need to get more data," he said. ## The holdout categories are the expensive ones Electricity, rent, hospital services, and car repairs have all been rising faster than 3% over the past six months, after adjusting for seasonal swings. Gasoline is up about 34% from a year ago. Together, the categories still above the line make up at least 60% of the CPI basket, which the BLS weights by how much households spend on each item. Groceries show the other side of the problem. Grocery prices rose less than 2% over the past year, yet they're still up nearly a third since December 2019. Electricity is up 43% over the same stretch. BLS, Yahoo Finance Slower inflation means prices rise more slowly. It doesn't bring them back down, and the Fed has no intention of returning to 2019

items.excerpt: After more than three decades of Republican dominance, Democrats in Texas see a rare chance to break through in November's midterm elections, as voter anger over immigration raids and the cost of living tests US President Donald Trump's support. No Democrat has won statewide office in the conservative southern state since 1994, and Trump carried Texas by nearly 14 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. But with a US Senate seat and the governorship at stake on November 3, recent polls suggest Republicans face an unusually competitive challenge. At the forefront is James Talarico, a 37-year-old former teacher and state lawmaker whose blend of Christian faith, economic populism and appeals for political unity has helped make the Senate race one of the country's most closely watched. A University of Texas poll released this week put Talarico ahead of Republican Ken Paxton, the state's attorney general and a staunch Trump ally, by 50 percent to 47 percent -- a lead within the survey's margin of error. A separate UMass Lowell poll found the two candidates tied.

items.title: Jesse Eisenberg, Julianne Moore bring curtain down on London Film Festival with 'The Debut' | Hollywood
items.excerpt: Published on: Oct 19, 2026, 06:26:56 IST Reuters ... * Eisenberg says he wrote 'The Debut' with Julianne Moore in mind Jesse Eisenberg, Julianne Moore bring curtain down on London Film Festival with 'The Debut' * The filmmaker wrote seven original songs for the movie's musical-within-a-film, 'Nosy Neighbours' * Eisenberg says his experiences in community theatre inspired the story ... LONDON, - Actor-filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg said he wrote the lead role in his musical comedy "The Debut" with Julianne Moore in mind, praising the Oscar-winning star as "the greatest actress in the world" as the film closed the London Film Festival on Sunday. "I just thought, this is Julianne Moore, and I will write every scene with her in mind and what she likes to do and what she's great at," Eisenberg, who wrote the screenplay and directed the film, told Reuters on the red carpet. ... Moore stars as Mona, a shy New Jersey housewife who is thrilled to land a role in a community theatre musical. Drawn to the experience by a longing for something missing in her life, Mona finds purpose and community through the show. ... The film, which marks Eisenberg's latest directing effort following his BAFTA-winning screenplay for "A Real Pain", features seven original songs written by the filmmaker. The numbers appear in the fictional stage production "Nosy Neighbours", a deliberately light-hearted, 1990s-inspired musical performed by a cast including "The Little Mermaid" star Halle Bailey. "I love songwriting, I love musical theatre music and I wrote these songs in earnest," Eisenberg said. ... "The Debut" brought the curtain down on the 70th London Film Festival, where Ukrainian filmmaker Sergei Loznitsa's "Imperium" won Best Film in the Official Competition.

Taylor Swift performed “The Fate of Ophelia” live for the first time Saturday at the star-studded Academy Museum Gala. Conan O’Brien introduced Swift prior to her four-song set, calling her “John, Paul, George, and Ringo all in one” before she and her band launched in “Blank Space.” Following that, Swift told the audience that they were about to witness the debut performance of a Life of a Showgirl track. > 🚨| Taylor Swift performing "The Fate of Ophelia" ... “This song, which we are playing for the very first time for you beautiful people, this is called ‘The Fate of Ophelia,'” Swift told the crowd. ... Swift then performed her Toy Story 5 contribution “I Knew It, I Knew You” before ending her gala performance with “Love Story.” ... Swift is an avowed film fan and is reportedly working on feature-length directorial debut. (The movie was announced in 2022, but still no word yet on when it might go into production or see release.) But her decision to play the Academy Museum’s annual gala also comes at an important moment: Right before the start of Oscars voting season.

items.title: Harry Styles’ MSG Residency Doc From John Wilson in the Works
items.excerpt: # Harry Styles’ MSG Residency Documentary in the Works From John Wilson The film will chronicle the pop star's 30-night run at the iconic New York City venue. ... The 32-year-old pop star has tapped filmmaker John Wilson to chronicle his 30-night run at the iconic New York City venue, which began Aug. 26 and wraps Oct. 31. ... The documentary was first reported by Variety on Saturday (Oct. 17), and Billboard has since confirmed the news. ... The film will blend live performances with a glimpse into Styles’ world, alongside authentic stories from those involved in the tour — from the singer and his fans to the many people working behind the scenes, according to Variety. ... The documentary is being produced by Universal Pictures Content Group, Peanut World Pictures and Styles. A potential theatrical release is reportedly in the works. ... Styles is currently performing in support of his fourth studio album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally., which debuted at No. 1 on both the Billboard 200 and the Official U.K. Albums Chart. The set’s lead single, “Aperture,” also topped the charts on both sides of the Atlantic. ... After stops in Amsterdam, London, São Paulo, Mexico City, Melbourne and Sydney, Styles is approaching the end of his 30-night MSG residency, with more Together, Together tour dates scheduled through August 2027. ... The tour’s 25-date extension next year launches in Phoenix on April 2, with subsequent stops in Dallas, Los Angeles, Toronto, Atlanta and Chicago. The European leg begins in Berlin on July 2 and includes dates in Paris, Madrid, Rome and Dublin before concluding with the final of three shows at London’s Wembley Stadium on Aug. 28.
